subject: Clarify billing for long-context hybrid sessions — minimums & exception
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, BrightLeaf Health Purchasing <purchasing@brightleafhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing questions on hybrid sessions / long context minimums

Hi Tessa,

Quick question as we pull together cost projections for the pilot: our workload will have a mix of long-context batch requests (20–40k tokens) and short streaming interactions that reference session context cached from earlier long calls. Two things we want to confirm so we can model commit sizing:

- How are billing units calculated when a single session contains both a long prefix (uploaded once) and multiple short streaming tokens? Do you charge the full context length on each subsequent streaming call or only the incremental tokens?
- Do you enforce a per-request or per-session minimum billing quantum? If so, how does that interact with prefix/KV cache discounts? For example, if the long call sets a 30k token context and then we do 30 short follow-ups of 25 tokens each, is there a repeated minimum applied each time?

We have language in procurement about committing to 250M tokens/month for the pilot; want to avoid surprise rounding causing big overages. If you have a short explainer or example calculations it would be great.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that's easier.

Best,
Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of ML Ops, BrightLeaf Health
attachments: BrightLeaf_MA-MVP_SOW_v3.pdf (attached)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Health Purchasing <purchasing@brightleafhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing questions on hybrid sessions / long context minimums

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear examples, that helps. High-level answers up front, then examples below.

Short answer: we meter and bill on a per-request token basis, with two important considerations that affect how that looks for hybrid sessions:

1) Prefix/KV caching: when the long context is cached within a session (KV cache/prefix cache), we do NOT re-charge the customer for the cached prefix tokens on each subsequent incremental request. The billed units are the new tokens generated/consumed on the incremental calls, plus a small overhead for cache-management metadata (typically <0.1% of the session tokens in practice).

2) Minimum quantum / rounding: we round billed units to our billing quantum (default: 64-token increment) per request. We also have a session-level minimum that only applies to ephemeral sessions (session pricing) — for long-lived pinned contexts we do not re-apply a per-request minimum to each short follow-up if the prefix is cached.

Example (rough):
- Initial upload / long call: 30,000 tokens -> billed as 30,000 tokens (subject to any negotiated per-token price)
- 30 short follow-ups at 25 tokens each: billed as 30 * 25 = 750 tokens (rounded per request to 64-token quantum -> effectively 30 * 64 = 1,920 billed tokens)
- With prefix caching enabled, the 30k prefix is not billed again. If you bundle short follow-ups in a single request we can avoid repeated rounding.

Summary: your primary driver of excess rounding in this pattern is the per-request quantum. Two practical mitigations are: 1) batch short interactions where possible; 2) we can negotiate a different billing quantum for the pilot (e.g., 16-token quantum) or provide a rounding credit.

I attached a small csv with example calculations using your numbers (billing_example.csv). I'm looping in Aditya on commercial concessions — Aditya, can you advise whether we can offer a temporary lowered quantum or rounding credit for BrightLeaf's pilot?

If helpful I can schedule a 30m next week to run through the numbers with your procurement team.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Billing questions on hybrid sessions / long context minimums — commercial ask

Aditya / Neha — forwarding BrightLeaf's question and my initial response. Key ask from procurement: avoid per-short-call rounding driving unexpected overages for pilot; they're committed to 250M tokens/mo but worried about micro-billing. Options I think we can offer (pick one):

A) Temporary pilot concession: reduce billing quantum from 64 -> 16 tokens for first 3 months, plus a 5% usage credit applied monthly to offset rounding.
B) Rounding credit: keep 64-token quantum, but apply a monthly rounding credit calculated as sum(rounded_billed - actual_token_usage) capped at 3% of monthly invoice.
C) Session pricing: convert their pilot to pinned-session pricing for long contexts where we bill the initial 30k and then bill follow-ups as pure incremental tokens with rounding applied per 1,024-token buckets instead of per-request — removes per-call noise but requires minimum committed capacity.

Commercial constraints:
- We can approve A for pilots under $20k/month ARR without additional approval. Anything above that needs Sales Ops sign-off.
- B is lower risk but requires Ops to compute the monthly rounding credit — Neha, do we have a quick script to produce the rounding delta per customer?
- C requires Dedicated or Private deployment conversation; for pilots we can emulate pinned-session behavior via sticky routing but need to validate latency SLOs.

Attached: BrightLeaf_MA-MVP_SOW_v3.pdf (their SOW) — they included sample volumes.

Recommend we offer A for the pilot (easy to explain, immediate reduction in perceived overage risk) and schedule a short technical call to show batching/SDK patterns that eliminate the majority of rounding. Thoughts?

—Tessa
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Health Purchasing <purchasing@brightleafhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing questions on hybrid sessions / long context minimums

Hi Maria — thanks again for the clear examples and for sharing the SOW. After internal review we can do the following for the pilot period (90 days):

- Reduce billing quantum to 16 tokens for BrightLeaf's pilot for the first 90 days.
- Additionally apply a 4% monthly rounding credit (applied to the invoice as a line item) to cover any residual micro-billing effects.
- We'll provide a short SDK pattern document and a sample config to demonstrate batching short follow-ups server-side to minimize per-request rounding — this will usually remove >80% of the rounding delta.

Next steps:
1) I'll send a one-page amendment to the SOW (attached) and a DocuSign link for signature (DocuSign: envelope-0a1b2c3d).
2) Technical walkthrough: propose Tues 22nd May 10:00am PT — I'll include our solutions engineer to show the batching knob and session pinning.

If these terms work, Maria, can you confirm and I'll route the amendment for signature?

Best,
—Tessa
